title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option 31: Weimar and Nazi Germany, 1918–39

topics.title: 1 The origins of the Republic, 1918–19
points: Situation in Germany at the end of the War: **political unrest, abdication of the Kaiser, armistice & new republic.**
**Strengths & weaknesses** of the new Weimar Constitution

topics.title: 2 The early challenges to the Weimar Republic, 1919–23
points: Causes of **early unpopularity of the Republic** (incl. the **'stab in the back' theory** & the key terms of the **Treaty of Versailles**)
Challenges to the Republic from Left & Right: **Spartacists, Freikorps, the Kapp Putsch.**
Challenges of 1923: **hyperinflation**; the reasons for & effects of, the **French occupation of the Ruhr**

topics.title: 3 The 'Golden Years': recovery of the Republic, 1924–29
points: Causes of economic recovery (incl. **Stresemann**, the **Rentenmark**, the **Dawes & Young Plans** & American loans & investment)
Stresemann's achievements in gaining **international acceptance of Germany** abroad through the **Locarno Pact** & joining the **League of Nations**

topics.title: 4 Changes in society, 1924–29
points: Changes in the **standard of living**
Changes in the **position of women** in work, politics & leisure
**Cultural changes**: developments in architecture, art & the cinema

sections.title: Key topic 2: Hitler's rise to power, 1919–33

topics.title: 1 Early development of the Nazi Party, 1920–22
points: Hitler's early career: **joining the German Workers' Party** & **setting up the Nazi Party, 1919–20**
**Twenty-Five Point Programme**; The **role of the SA**

topics.title: 2 The Munich Putsch and the Nazi Party, 1923–28
points: Reasons for, events & consequences of the **Munich Putsch**; ***Mein Kampf***
Causes of **limited support for the Nazi Party, 1924–28**; Party reorganisation (incl. the **Bamberg Conference of 1926**)

topics.title: 3 The growth in support for the Nazis, 1929–32
points: **Growth of unemployment** – its causes & impact; growth of support for the **Communist Party**
Causes of **growth in support for the Nazi Party** (incl. the **appeal of Hitler & the Nazis**, the **effects of propaganda** & the **work of the SA**)

topics.title: 4 How Hitler became Chancellor, 1932–33
points: **Presidential & Reichstag elections of 1932**; Causes of **Hitler becoming Chancellor in 1933** (incl. the roles of **Hindenburg** & **von Papen**)

sections.title: Key topic 3: Nazi control and dictatorship, 1933–39

topics.title: 1 The creation of a dictatorship, 1933–34
points: **Reichstag Fire**; The **Enabling Act** & the **banning of other parties & trade unions**
**Threat from Röhm & the SA**, the **Night of the Long Knives**; The **death of Hindenburg**; Hitler becomes **Führer**, the **army oath of allegiance**

topics.title: 2 The police state
points: **Gestapo**, the **SS** & **concentration camps**
Nazi control of the **legal system**

topics.title: 3 Controlling and influencing attitudes
points: **Goebbels** & the **Ministry of Propaganda**: **censorship**, Nazi **use of media, rallies & sport** (incl. the **Berlin Olympics (1936)**)
Nazi control of **culture & the arts** (incl. art, architecture, literature & film)
Nazi attempts to control the Catholic & Protestant Churches: the **Concordat** & the **Reich Church**

topics.title: 4 Opposition, resistance and conformity
points: **Extent of support** for the Nazi regime
**Opposition from the Churches** (incl. **Pastor Niemöller**)
**Opposition from the young** (incl. the **Swing Youth** & the **Edelweiss Pirates**)

sections.title: Key topic 4: Life in Nazi Germany, 1933–39

topics.title: 1 Nazi policies towards women
points: Nazi **views on women & the family**
Nazi **policies towards women** (incl. **marriage & family, employment & appearance**)

topics.title: 2 Nazi policies towards the young
points: Nazi **aims & policies towards the young**; The **Hitler Youth** & the **League of German Maidens**
Nazi **control of the young through education** (incl. the **curriculum & teachers**)

topics.title: 3 Employment and living standards
points: Nazi **policies to reduce unemployment**: **labour service, autobahns, rearmament** & **invisible unemployment**
Changes in the **standard of living**, especially of German workers; The **Labour Front, Strength Through Joy, Beauty of Labour**

topics.title: 4 The persecution of minorities
points: Nazi **racial beliefs & policies** & the treatment of minority groups: **Slavs, Roma & Sinti, homosexuals & people with disabilities**
**Persecution of Jewish people** (incl. the **boycott of Jewish shops & businesses (1933)**, the **Nuremberg Laws** & **'Kristallnacht'**)
